game: BUF @ CAR, 2025-10-26 13:00 ET, outdoor, CAR +7, total 47.5

script.base: Market script is a one-score Bills lead, not a shootout: implied totals BUF 27.2 / CAR 20.2 on 47.5. Buffalo should be ahead by the second half and lean on James Cook (54 carries, 253 yards in weeks 4-6) plus Josh Allen's legs (19/143) late. Carolina's offense is Rico Dowdle (70 carries, 468 rush yards and 11 targets for 101 yards in weeks 5-7), but Bryce Young is Doubtful (ankle), so they may be stuck on early-down runs even as a +7 dog rather than freely throwing. Khalil Shakir is Buffalo's chain-mover (19 targets, 147 yards, only 72 air).
script.flip1: Buffalo jumps up two scores early, clocks out, and pass volume for Shakir, Keon Coleman and Dalton Kincaid stalls while Cook's carries stay up. Carolina then abandons the run, Dowdle's rush workload dies, and a backup QB's late throws are the only CAR volume.
script.flip2: Carolina hangs around because Buffalo allows 5.80 yards per carry. Dowdle keeps them on schedule, both teams stay run-heavy, and the WR overs (Tetairoa McMillan 62.5, Shakir 45.5) are the legs that miss.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, not final inactives (90-minute scratch list not in pack). CAR QB Bryce Young Doubtful (ankle): no backup QB named, so CAR WR/TE connections (McMillan, Xavier Legette, Tommy Tremble, Hunter Renfrow) lose certainty and early-down work funnels further to Dowdle if Young sits or is one-legged; Chuba Hubbard does not automatically inherit the job (14 carries, 31 yards in weeks 5-7 vs Dowdle's 70/468). BUF WR Josh Palmer Out (knee): his weeks 4-6 slice was 7 targets, 121 yards, 113 air, which redistributes toward Shakir first, then Coleman (already 17 targets but only 79 yards) and Dawson Knox if Kincaid is limited. BUF TE Dalton Kincaid Questionable (oblique): do not bet his 48.5; if he sits or is snapped down, Shakir/Knox gain short-middle targets. BUF DT DaQuan Jones Out (calf) plus LBs Matt Milano (pec) and Terrel Bernard (ankle) Questionable: interior and second-level run fit weakened, which helps Dowdle, not a CAR receiver. BUF S Taylor Rapp Out (knee) and CB Maxwell Hairston Questionable (knee): missing safety helps deep shots (McMillan 222 air yards in L3) only if Young can throw. No CAR skill-position out on the report.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Cannot map Shakir, Coleman, Kincaid, McMillan or Dowdle to a named zone defender. step limitation: coverage shell unknown.
matchup.pressure: CAR blitzes only 23%. Buffalo EPA/dropback is 0.29 with no blitz vs 0.11 when blitzed, so a light Carolina rush lets Allen work the middle when Buffalo does throw, and it does not force a checkdown-only game. Buffalo blitzes 32%. Carolina EPA/dropback is -0.23 vs blitz and 0.04 vs none, so pressure that gets home kills McMillan/Legette deep yards and should bump Dowdle and Tremble checkdowns.
matchup.bleeds: CAR defense (7 games): rush 4.31 YPC, only 13 runs of 10+; pass YPA left 6.98 (99), middle 9.51 (45), right 4.89 (76); 19 plays of 20+ for 231 yards. They bleed the middle, not the right side, and they are not a run sieve. BUF defense (6 games): rush 5.80 YPC and 31 runs of 10+; pass YPA left 6.36 (61), middle 7.04 (26), right 6.62 (78); 15 plays of 20+ for 180 yards. The Bills bleed the run, with Jones out widening that hole.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Dowdle, the CAR run game, into a Bills run defense at 5.80 YPC missing DaQuan Jones. Buffalo's primary target Shakir (short/middle, 72 air on 19 targets) does overlap CAR's middle bleed (9.51 YPA), but his 45.5 line sits on top of last4 45, 69, 45, 33, so that overlap is not a priced edge here. Coleman (205 air, 79 yards) is the deep guy, not the middle leak. McMillan (222 air) would overlap Rapp's absence, but Young Doubtful blocks that overlap.

Dowdle last4 rush yards 32, 206, 183, 79 and weeks 5-7 total 70/468 (about 156 per game) with 11 targets/101 receiving yards; the 32 is the only recent game that does not crush 32.5. Hubbard last4 rush 38, 73, 49, 31, but weeks 5-7 total only 14 carries and 31 yards, so the 73 cannot be inside that L3 window and the current role is a backup. Cook last4 rush 108, 117, 49, 87 (L3 54/253, about 84 per game) with Allen also rushing 19/143; 97.5 is above the recent pace. Shakir last4 45, 69, 45, 33 vs 45.5. Coleman last4 20, 45, 23, 11 vs 24.5 on terrible yards per target. Kincaid last4 37, 66, 28, 108 and only 8 targets in weeks 4-6, plus oblique Q. McMillan last4 62, 73, 29, 33 (L3 18 targets, 135 yards, about 45 per game) vs 62.5. Legette last4 -2, 31, 11, 92. BUF offensive sample in the pack is weeks 4-6 only, not 5-7.

Script-dependent on it not becoming a blowout; the +7 base case and the low bar still survive a modest trail.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because the one role assumption broke, not because the Bills suddenly stopped the run. Buffalo led by multiple scores at half, Carolina could not stay on schedule with Young either inactive or ineffective, and the staff abandoned Dowdle before he cleared a number as low as 32.5, finishing in the high 20s on a short carry count. Hubbard then caught a long draw against the 5.80 YPC front in leftover snaps and cleared 49.5, so both legs lost together. The other way the over loses is a late Dowdle inactive that this morning report does not show. The counter-case is stronger on price than on football: 32.5 and 49.5 are season-median stand-ins, not shopped closes, so there may never have been a bettable edge. That is why the slip is flagged, not sized. It is not stronger than the weeks 5-7 carry split on the field, so the Dowdle read is not dropped.
slip_story: One story only: Carolina's run hierarchy into a Bills run funnel. Dowdle over 32.5 is the bellcow against 5.80 YPC and a missing starting DT; Hubbard under 49.5 is the snap casualty of that same story. Young Doubtful keeps the slip from needing a pass-heavy dog script. Do not mix in McMillan, Legette, Shakir or Coleman overs, a total under, or any TD. Two legs, one market per player. Both die if Dowdle does not play the role, so it is a correlated pair, not two independent edges.
